A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TEOChat model and TEOChatlas dataset. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original TEOChat training and evaluation results, including temporal benchmarks, model ablations, zero-shot transfer, and single-image evaluations in Tables 1–5 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds captioning, grounding, image-reference, and temporal-sampling experiments in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The shared CLIP encoder, MLP connector, Llama 2 decoder, image references, and LoRA training remain unchanged. Although v2 removes the statement that the projector is frozen, v1 Figure 3 and Table 2 already indicate projector fine-tuning; this reconciles the description rather than establishes a new method.

E1.justification: v2 adds fine-tuned and zero-shot captioning evaluation on UCM-Captions, Sydney-Captions, and RSICD (Appendix I.2). Section 5.6 also adds qualitative test scenarios involving temporal recognition of vehicles and airplanes and seasonal differences. The original TEOChatlas composition and temporal benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds InternVL2-4B and Qwen2VL-7B-Instruct to the existing multi-image comparison. Table 5 adds RSVQA, RSGPT, LHRS-Bot, and VHM. New captioning and grounding tables introduce further reported comparators, including MiniGPT-v2, Shikra, and captioning specialists.

E3.justification: xBD localization changes from IoU to per-pixel F1 (v1 Appendix G; v2 Appendix H). New protocols include separate caption fine-tuning for 5, 20, and 5 epochs, zero-shot caption evaluation with multiple language-generation metrics, and Acc@0.5 grounding with a 224-by-224 GeoChat control. The original base training procedure is retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation separating the effects of Image 1 and Image 2 references, grounding analyses by object size and input resolution, repeated temporal-sequence sampling, and qualitative task-generalization cases. The original QFabric test-time identifier ablation remains unchanged as Table 10, formerly Table 9.

E5.justification: New Table 20 reports five evaluations using different random eight-image samples on fMoW RGB and Sentinel, exposing sampling variability absent from v1. These are sampling repetitions, not documented independent training runs; confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive captioning, grounding, and ablation results. For example, Table 19 reports overall grounding scores of 37.3 for TEOChat and 43.8 for GeoChat. Existing Table 1 also revises S2Looking detection from 33.6 to 34.5 and replaces xBD localization's 35.5 IoU with 38.9 F1; the latter is not a directly comparable performance gain.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, proofs, or derivations. The localization metric revision is an empirical evaluation change, without new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central temporal-VLM and instruction-dataset contributions remain. v2 explicitly includes captioning in the abstract's single-image performance claim and adds a claim of generalization to tasks not explicitly represented in training (Section 5.6), modestly extending the stated capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of gaps to state-of-the-art specialists, comparator failure patterns, and Image 2 references as boundaries between visual tokens. Appendix I discusses caption-benchmark defects and the grounding disadvantage associated with lower resolution. These materially expand the explanation of mechanisms, weaknesses, and applicability beyond v1's localization discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix E expands prompt-format documentation; Appendix I specifies caption fine-tuning budgets and positional-embedding interpolation for the reduced-resolution GeoChat control. Section 7 explicitly identifies training and evaluation resources at the already disclosed repository. Core training hyperparameters and hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning across temporal EO modeling, natural-image VLMs, temporal VLMs, and EO assistants. It acknowledges concurrent CDChat and distinguishes its bitemporal scope from TEOChat's broader tasks and sequence lengths. The main results discussion also introduces stronger specialist reference points.

P1.justification: v2 tightens introductory and dataset prose, standardizes GeoChat Instruct terminology, updates headings and cross-references, and organizes supplementary results into Appendix I subsections. It adds generalization, reproducibility, and related-work sections while retaining the main narrative sequence and much existing wording.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands comparison tables and adds captioning, grounding, and robustness tables plus two new qualitative figures. Table 5 distinguishes fine-tuned results with italics. Existing temporal examples move from Figure 4 to Figure 6, and the single-image illustration labeled Table 10 in v1 becomes Figure 7.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence and boundaries of the generalist-capability claims through broader baselines, systematic captioning evaluations, grounding results that expose weaknesses, and targeted robustness checks. Specialist and concurrent-work comparisons also improve positioning. Reporting flaws remain: S2Looking is 34.5 in Table 1 but 33.6 in Tables 2 and 4, and Section 5.4 swaps the new comparators' improvement margins. These limit confidence in exact margins but do not overturn the substantial gains in empirical support and qualification.
